tasks.instruction: Given tenths of a second elapsed on a 24-second shot clock, return the whole seconds remaining, rounded up.
tasks.note: Ceiling division; adding 10 instead of 9 overshoots on exact multiples.

tasks.instruction: Tempo modes are numbered from 1, and mode 1 is the first tempo in the table; return that tempo times the number of bars.
tasks.note: Index shift by one; the wrong edit reverses the table instead.

tasks.instruction: Subtract the discount from the subtotal first, then add the tax percentage computed on the discounted amount.
tasks.note: Billing: tax must be on the discounted amount; the wrong edit still taxes the full subtotal.

tasks.instruction: A player can be hit when neither the shield (bit 0) nor invisibility is set; invisibility is bit 3 (value 8).
tasks.note: Shift distance selects the flag bit; value 8 is bit 3, not bit 4.

tasks.instruction: Scale grams from the old number of servings (third argument) to the new one (second argument), rounding to the nearest gram with halves rounded up.
tasks.note: Cooking: half the divisor is added after multiplying, not before.

tasks.instruction: Seats are numbered from 0 with six seats per row (columns 0 to 5); return true for window seats, the first and last column.
tasks.note: Travel: the last column is 5; comparing the raw seat number only works in row 0.

tasks.instruction: Add the bonus (third argument) to the score at the given position instead of overwriting it, and return the updated scores.
tasks.note: Games: read-modify-write of an array element; index wraps modulo 4.

tasks.instruction: The damage-over-time effect lasts four ticks, halving each tick; return the total damage over all four ticks.
tasks.note: Fold count is the number of ticks.

tasks.instruction: The machine should keep handing out quarters for as long as at least 25 cents remain, then return the cents left over.
tasks.note: Loop cap was 3 quarters; inputs up to a few dollars need a larger cap.

tasks.instruction: Return the index of the first time slot whose bookings exceed the capacity, scanning from slot 0; return 6 if none does.
tasks.note: Scheduling: the scan started at slot 1; the wrong edit also treats a full slot as overbooked.

tasks.instruction: Return how many hourly doublings the dough needs to reach at least the goal volume; dough already at the goal needs zero hours.
tasks.note: Record state (volume, hours); the hour counter started at 1.

tasks.instruction: Count how many of the five songs, taken in order, fit into the time budget; all five songs must be considered.
tasks.note: Music: loop cap must equal the playlist length; a song that exactly fills the budget still fits.

tasks.instruction: The traffic light has three phases (0, 1, 2) and wraps from 2 back to 0; return the phase after the given number of ticks.
tasks.note: State machine; the phase count passed to the step was 4. Ticks are at most 50.

tasks.instruction: The lock should open only when all four entered digits match the code.
tasks.note: The loop result is the count of leading matching digits; a full match is 4.

tasks.instruction: Scores 0-19 get F, 20-39 D, 40-59 C, 60-79 B and 80 or more A; return the letter's byte. The letter table is in the wrong order.
tasks.note: Fixing the table while dropping the cap makes 100 wrap to F.

tasks.instruction: The ticket code is the sum of all letters of the station name plus the seat number, modulo 100; every letter must be included.
tasks.note: OSLO bytes sum to 317; folding 5 times wraps and counts O twice.

tasks.instruction: Read the word from its end: position 0 is the last letter, position 3 the first. Keep the upper-case option as it is.
tasks.note: Text processing: reversed index is length minus one minus position.

tasks.instruction: The menu string stores each item's price as a digit character; return that price in dollars times the quantity.
tasks.note: Cooking menu: subtract the code of '0' (48) before multiplying.

tasks.instruction: Transpose the note up by the given steps on the seven-note scale; add 100 for every octave crossed, where an octave is seven steps from C.
tasks.note: Music: octave carry divides the absolute position by the scale length 7.

tasks.instruction: Read the bill amount and write the amount plus a 15 percent tip (rounded down), not the tip alone.
tasks.note: Billing echo; adding a flat 15 instead of the computed tip is the wrong edit.

tasks.instruction: Read the two teams' goals and write the larger count first and the smaller second.
tasks.note: Sports scoreboard; the wrong edit writes the smaller first.

tasks.instruction: Read the counts of three storage bins (not two) and write their total.
tasks.note: Inventory; the token must be threaded through the third read.

tasks.instruction: After writing the hand of three cards, also write the total of the three card values.
tasks.note: Card game; puts writes the length 3 first; the total must come after the hand.

tasks.instruction: Read a Celsius temperature and emit it in Fahrenheit: multiply by 9, divide by 5, then add 32.
tasks.note: Signals: the offset is added after scaling; the token goes through the helper.

tasks.instruction: Log the trip's speed (distance divided by time) first and then the distance, each through the stamp helper.
tasks.note: Travel log: division operands were swapped; the wrong edit fixes the division but swaps the stamp order.

tasks.instruction: Read a unit price and a quantity and write the receipt line [price, quantity, price times quantity] with puts.
tasks.note: Billing receipt; product wraps modulo 2^32.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that turns metres and seconds into seconds per kilometre, and make the target return the faster (smaller) pace of the two runners.
tasks.note: New helper pace; zero metres gives the all-ones pace, which is never the faster one.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper converting hours and minutes to minutes, and use it for both clock times so the target returns the minutes from the first time to the second.
tasks.note: Cooking timer; the start ignored the second time's minutes.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that says whether a stock is below the minimum, and make the target return true when exactly one of the two stocks is below it.
tasks.note: Inventory; a stock equal to the minimum is not below it.

tasks.instruction: Add a helper that scales a level by a percentage (multiply, then divide by 100), and use it so both the left and right channels are scaled.
tasks.note: Signals; dividing before multiplying loses precision.
